title: Hypergraph Generation via Structured Stochastic Diffusion
claim: Structured noising progressively smooths a structured object's incidence representation into a simple Gaussian base law, and a learned reverse process generates samples from it.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; example graph left, four-snapshot heatmap sequence with forward and reverse SDE arrows
description: The left panel shows a bipartite actor–movie hypergraph. Five black-and-white actor portraits (Bogart, Bergman, Rains, Lorre, Grant) sit at the top and are labeled 'Actors (Vertices)'. Three movie stills (Casablanca, The Maltese Falcon, Notorious) sit below and are labeled 'Movies (hyperedges)'. Thin black lines connect each actor to the movies they appear in. The right panel shows the incidence matrix H as a 5×3 heatmap with yellow and dark-navy cells. Three more heatmaps follow it left to right, labeled heat smoothing, heat + OU, and late conditional mean. They fade progressively to a uniform grey-olive. A forward SDE equation sits above a long right-pointing arrow marked s=0, small s, intermediate s and large s. A dashed grey reverse SDE arrow and equation run underneath, pointing left. A colorbar from 0 to 1 sits at the far right.
caption: Left: An actor--movie hypergraph. Right: Its incidence matrix $H$ and three snapshots of the conditional forward mean. Rows correspond to actors and columns to movies, with $H_{ij}=1$ if actor $i$ appears in movie $j$. Generation starts from the OU Gaussian base law [ref] and follows the learned reverse SDE.
abstract: Hypergraphs model higher-order interactions, but realistic hypergraph generation remains difficult because incidence, hyperedge-size heterogeneity, and overlap structure are not faithfully captured by pairwise reductions. We propose \HEDGE, a generative model defined directly on relaxed incidence matrices via a structured stochastic diffusion. The forward process combines a hypergraph-specific two-sided heat operator with an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck component, preserving structure-aware noising near the data while yielding an explicit Gaussian terminal law. Conditional on an observed hypergraph, this forward process is linear-Gaussian, so conditional means, covariances, scores, and reverse-drift targets are available in closed form. We therefore learn a permutation-equivariant state-only reverse-drift field in incidence space by regressing onto exact conditional targets, and generate samples by simulating a learned reverse-time SDE from the Gaussian base law. We establish exactness in the ideal state-only setting together with finite-horizon stability guarantees, and empirically show improved hypergraph generation quality relative to strong baselines.
